claims.text: The proposed material is an equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi exhibits superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared with conventional structural alloys.
CoCrFeMnNi forms a stable, multi-component protective oxide layer during mechanical wear at elevated temperatures.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy is homogenized and solution heat-treated.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a single-phase microstructure.
A uniform microstructure promotes formation of a dense, multi-component surface oxide film under thermal and mechanical strain.
The multiple principal elements in the HEA promote formation of a stable and adherent oxide layer.
The stable and adherent oxide layer impedes further oxidation and corrosion.
Homogeneous elemental distribution reduces localized degradation under tribological stress.
Under the specified conditions, the HEA will have lower weight loss than conventional alloys.
Under the specified conditions, the HEA will have lower rates of pitting and surface degradation than conventional alloys.
Under the specified conditions, the HEA will retain its mechanical properties better than conventional alloys.
Enhanced resistance is anticipated only when elevated temperature and tribological stress are both present.
The benefits may be less evident in static corrosive environments or at lower temperatures.
Direct experimental evidence for formation and protective efficacy of the oxide layer under simultaneous tribological, high-temperature, and corrosive conditions is lacking.
